subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool contract, and if so what provider-egress, fallback, and session/audit policy should govern that raw-media path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation would change core content types, provider routing, sensitive media egress, and transcript/replay semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit raw-media egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep read audio transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of the read tool and direct users to the existing tools.media.audio and infer audio transcribe paths until policy is settled.

options.title: Fold this into the broader native-audio tracker
options.body: Treat this read-tool request as a subcase of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 if maintainers want one native-audio product design thread.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit raw-media egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read/content contract and repeated adjacent media/provider contract work point to steipete as the best available routing owner for the product contract decision.
